subject: MAP: PoV environment gate and target close plan (API seeds, org setup, IP allowlist, VPC peering)
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@cardioai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoV MAP & environment gating — next steps

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. CardioAI is keen to run a short PoV to validate latency and cost for our inferencing workload. Our legal/procurement timeline is fairly tight — we'd like to do a 2-week PoV and aim to finalize commercial terms within three weeks.

Could you share a mutual action plan that lays out the environment gating steps (org seed, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering) plus dates for the PoV canary and final validation? Also attaching a short security checklist we started — there may be a SOC2 evidence request.

Attachment: CardioAI-security-asks.pdf (attachment stub)

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform
CardioAI

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cardioai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoV MAP & environment gating — next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear timeline. Draft MAP attached (mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx). High level proposal below — please confirm dates that work for you and procurement: 

- Week 0 (Apr 14-16): Org seed + service account creation (CardioAI provides admin contact for org seed).
- Week 1 (Apr 17-23): API keys issued (ephemeral keys for canary), IP allowlist configured (CardioAI will provide CIDR ranges).
- Week 2 (Apr 24-30): VPC peering setup & canary run (48-72 hours), performance sweep, final data export for cost analysis.
- Target close: commercial/PO signed by May 2 (we can compress if procurement is ready).

Questions/asks: 
1) Please confirm the CIDR ranges and whether you require bi-directional peering or a routed NAT setup.
2) Who is the procurement contact? (we'll send an initial SOW + T&Cs).

I'm looping in Marissa for the peering and API-key rotation details. If this schedule is too aggressive we can push the canary by a week.

(attachment: mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx)

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cardioai.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoV MAP & environment gating — tech notes on keys/peering

Alex — quick tech notes to make the gating smoother: 

- API key model: we'll provision short-lived API seeds tied to a CardioAI org id. Keys rotate by default every 72 hours for PoV; we'll give an option for 30-day tokens if your automation requires it.
- Org setup: we need a single org-admin email and a preferred org name (this controls telemetry and billing tags).
- IP allowlist: recommend submitting a minimal set of egress ranges (one /24 per region) to reduce ops friction. For the PoV, allowlist only from your peering subnet to limit exposure.
- VPC peering: we'll peer into us-west-2. Pre-reqs: your VPC CIDR (no overlap with our peered range 10.100.0.0/16) and confirmation that you can accept routes from our side. If you cannot peer, we can fall back to a private endpoint in your VPC.

I'll add a short runbook to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_MAP_PoV_CardioAI (see "peering-runbook.md").

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: peering-runbook.md)

From: Alex Rivera <alex@cardioai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoV MAP & environment gating — tech notes on keys/peering

Thanks Marissa — helpful. A couple of clarifications from our infra team: 

- We can provide a single /24 from our peering VPC (CIDR: 172.20.10.0/24). No overlap with 10.100.0.0/16. Bi-directional is fine.
- Procurement contact is procurement@cardioai.com (Lara Gomez will lead).
- For SOC2 evidence: we still need to collect your SOC2 Type II report (or a letter of attestation) before we enable any production-like token retention. I'll attach our formal SOC2 request as requested.

Can you confirm whether ephemeral keys will be sufficient for our canary (we plan to run a 24-hour high-QPS test) or whether we should request a longer-lived token for the stress window?

Attachment: SOC2-request.pdf (attachment stub)

— Alex

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cardioai.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoV MAP & environment gating — alignment and next steps

Alex/Lara — thanks for the procurement contact and CIDR. Quick alignment from Ops: 

- Org seed: please send org-admin email by EOD Apr 15. We'll provision the CardioAI org and seed a service account for the PoV.
- API keys: we'll issue two ephemeral keys (one for canary, one for smoke tests). For the 24-hour high-QPS run please approve a single 14-day token to avoid mid-run rotation interruptions — we'll log and audit all requests.
- IP allowlist: we have noted 172.20.10.0/24. Please confirm any additional egress/public IPs by Apr 16.
- VPC peering: Marissa will start the peering config on Apr 17 once routes are exchanged and the SIDs are confirmed. Expect peering establishment within 24 hours after route acceptance.
- SOC2: we'll provide a link to our latest SOC2 Type II by Apr 16 and a stub response to the CardioAI checklist in the Drive folder.

Next: Karthik will send the SOW + draft SLP to procurement@cardioai.com and cc the PoV MAP. I'll schedule a quick kick-off call for Apr 17 09:00 PT to run through the runbook and confirm routing. 

Thanks — we'll treat this as a priority to meet your close window.

Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
(attachments: mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx, SOC2-request.pdf)
